# Psalm 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. According to the Sheminith. A psalm of David.

**2** O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger, nor discipline me in Your wrath.

**3** Be gracious to me, O LORD, for I am languishing; heal me, O LORD, for my bones are troubled.

**4** My soul also is greatly troubled. But You, O LORD — how long?

**5** Turn, O LORD, deliver my soul; save me for the sake of Your steadfast love.

**6** For in death there is no remembrance of You; in Sheol who will give You thanks?

**7** I am weary with my moaning; every night I flood my bed with tears; I drench my couch with my weeping.

**8** My eye wastes away from grief; it grows weak because of all my foes.

**9** Depart from me, all you workers of evil, for the LORD has heard the sound of my weeping.

**10** The LORD has heard my plea; the LORD accepts my prayer.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- **6:1**: The first of the seven penitential psalms (6, 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, 143). Early church tradition grouped them for liturgical use.

- **6:7**: The hyperbolic imagery — flooding the bed, drenching the couch — conveys the intensity of grief through exaggeration.

— LOGOS
